The main takeaway from our work is that

the species composition of macroinvertebrate assemblages in the nearshore waters of the lower west coast varied among habitat types and, to a lesser extent, zones and seasons, in ways that matched the extents of their variations in the values for the seven enduring environmental characteristics that had been used to distinguish those habitat types.

the species composition of benthic assemblages in nearshore waters is influenced by the enduring physical characteristics of their habitat, which in turn influence their exposure to waves, and the associated physical and chemical conditions, and that the assemblage composition is not greatly affected by the seasonal changes in water temperature and the availability of food.

the assemblages and abundances of benthic invertebrates in near-shore waters are strongly affected by the extent of exposure to wave activity, which determines the nature of the sediment and the extent of the input of organic matter.
